subject: Urgent: quantization upgrade causing throughput & error spikes
messages:
From: Tim Jensen <tim.jensen@acme-health.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production regression after model quant upgrade

Neha —

We pushed the model variant you suggested (rlm-3b-q4_2.1) last night in canary and then roll‑out to prod at 02:00 PT. Since then we've seen a steady rise in 5xxs and a ~2.8x increase in tail latency for our clinical summarization pipeline. Error rate went from 0.2% to ~3.7% and throughput dropped ~26% despite no change in traffic.

We attached a handful of traces and an aggregated throughput CSV. The errors look like OOM-like worker restarts and also a few malformed JSON outputs that break our downstream parsers. Screenshot and logs attached.

This is impacting incoming referrals tonight — engineering is on standby. Can you escalate? We need either a rollback or a mitigation plan within the next 6 hours.

Attachments: profile-traces.zip, error_snippets.log, throughput-summary.csv

—Tim
Tim Jensen

Acme Health

On it. Initial findings from infra quick look:
- Workers show repeated exits with 'cuda out of memory' followed by autoscaler restarting pods. Memory footprint for rlm-3b-q4_2.1 is ~18% higher at 512-token windows compared to prior q4_1.
- We see a hot‑spot in GEMM kernel selection for ffn that increased per-token CPU on host fallback.
- Some inference tasks are hitting fallback path that emits truncated JSON occasionally — will paste sample below.

Suggested immediate mitigations:
- Roll back to rlm-3b-q4_1 for the affected customer route (canary -> prod path) to restore baseline.
- Disable the new kernel selector for models with sequence length > 256 while we debug.

I can prepare the rollback patch and a playbook for Marissa to execute. If Neha wants exec loop-in, say the word and I'll include performance impact numbers.

Sample quoted output (from error_snippets.log):
\"{\"summary\": \"Patient presents with chest pain...\" Truncated JSON\"\"

Subject: Fwd: Urgent: quantization upgrade causing throughput & error spikes — exec update

Team — brief update for execs and follow-up actions. TL;DR: a quantization profile variant (rlm-3b-q4_2.1) triggered increased memory usage and a kernel fallback that elevated per-token CPU and introduced intermittent truncated outputs. The regression impacted Acme Health production for ~5.5 hours before rollback.

Timeline / impact:
- 2026-06-29 02:00 PT — rlm-3b-q4_2.1 rolled to prod by Acme's canary plan.
- 02:30–08:00 PT — elevated 5xxs, p99 latency ~2.8x baseline, throughput down ~26%; parsing failures at ~3.7% of requests.
- 10:30 PT — Redwood rollback to rlm-3b-q4_1 completed; metrics returned to baseline within 12 minutes of rollback.

Root cause (preliminary):
- Quantization changes in q4_2.1 altered kernel selection heuristics; for long sequences the runtime fell back to a less-efficient execution path that increased memory working set and CPU.
- There is a gap in the pre-rollout perf profile smoke tests: sequence-length distributions in customer traffic were not captured, so the regression did not show in our standard canary metrics.

Immediate remediation:
- Hotfix: pin per-route model variant configs to previous quant profile until we ship a kernel selector fix.
- Short-term: extend canary smoke tests to include high-seq traffic patterns and memory pressure scenarios.
- Mid-term: add an automated quant-profile perf guard that rejects variants that increase memory or p99 latency beyond an acceptable delta.

Customer comms and commercial:
- I've proposed a proactive apology email and a credit commensurate with 6 hours of impacted service; commercial to decide.
- Marissa will provide a post-mortem write-up by EOD Friday and include action owners.

Requests for execs:
- Please approve a one-time SLA credit framework up to $Xk for incidents of this class so we can close the loop quickly.
- Approval to prioritize kernel selector and canary test improvements on next sprints.

Attaching the INF ticket and traces: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4821 and drive folder.

—Neha
Head of Account Success, Redwood Inference
